subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should external source chats keep automatic bare-text visible replies by default, or should OpenClaw require explicit message-tool/final-only delivery for user-visible output on channel sessions?
rationale: The code choice trades a security-sensitive internal-text leak against compatibility for existing users and models that rely on automatic final text replies, so automation should not choose the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Adopt explicit delivery with migration
options.body: Make external channel/session output explicit or final-only by default, preserve a documented opt-out or migration path for deployments that need legacy automatic bare-text replies, and cover cron plus streaming paths.

options.title: Keep automatic default with stronger guards
options.body: Preserve compatibility by default while adding narrower suppression for known commentary, reasoning, NO_REPLY, and pre-tool block shapes, accepting that some malformed bare text may still require follow-up fixes.

options.title: Opt-in only for now
options.body: Leave the existing automatic default, improve docs and diagnostics, and unblock only users who configure message-tool-only or final-tag enforcement.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit delivery with migration
recommendation.body: Make external channel/session output explicit or final-only by default, preserve a documented opt-out or migration path for deployments that need legacy automatic bare-text replies, and cover cron plus streaming paths.
